node.title: Re: next unless condition
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [hankcoder],

Yes, that's essentially what it means - next unless $cell; does the same as unless($cell) {next}, and unless is just an if with the condition inverted, as in if (not ...) .... This is covered in [doc://perlsyn#Compound-Statements] and [doc://perlsyn#Statement-Modifiers].

Another way to write that is $cell or next; which means that if $cell has a true value, the or expression will be true, so it "short-circuits" and does not need to execute the right hand side, next. If $cell is false, the or needs to check its right argument for truth, so the next is executed.

You can see this equivalence yourself with [doc://B::Deparse]:

$ perl -MO=Deparse,-p -e 'next unless $cell' ($cell or (next));

Hope that helps,
-- Hauke D
